text:
alex: Morning handoff from me — I'm primary for the 07:00-15:00 shift. Quick summary: we had a KV-cache-induced throttle alert overnight, several customers saw elevated 429/503s between 02:10-03:05. Incident is resolved from a customer-impact perspective but there are follow-ups.

sam: Key points I picked up while on-call:
- Root cause: a regressed change in the batcher that reduced cache evictions under churn, leading to cache pressure and downstream queueing.
- Observable: burst of `cache_fill_time` and `batch_latency` increase, autoscaler didn't react fast enough due to a conservative cool-down.
- Impact: short-lived degraded tail latency for interactive requests; some retry churn caused increased token-cost and transient 5xx.

incidentbot: [pager] PAGER fired: kv-cache-throttle - 02:12 UTC - 65 pages. Severity: P2. Linked incident: INC-2026-249.

li: Actions taken overnight: rolled back the risky batcher patch at 02:25, increased batcher autoscale headroom (temp), and enabled fallback to smaller-batch execution for known heavy routes. Also applied a throttle circuit on the most aggressive customers to reduce retry storms.

maya: Current status:
- User-visible errors: 0 active reports since 03:10.
- Metrics: `5xx_rate` back to baseline, `p95 latency` still ~20% above baseline on a few routes.
- Capacity: we have +2 reserved nodes in the autoscale group (manual); monitoring will autoscale afterwards.

alex: Primary->Sam, secondary->Li for the next 2 hours while I wrap context with infra. Coverage gap: no one on pager for infra-compile during 11:00-12:00 (internal meeting block). Need someone to cover that window or say yes to being on-call for compile.

sam: I can cover compile 11:00-12:00 if no objections.

li: I'll own follow-ups on the runbook items. I opened a tracking ticket: RW-OPS-1298.

alex: Runbook pointers (short):
- KV Cache pressure: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure (steps: reduce batch size -> enable per-route fallback -> scale nodes -> notify customers).
- Hot rollback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hot-rollback (how to pin model versions and revert mesh config).
- Pager triage checklist: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/pager-triage.

sam: Short playbook commands used overnight:
```bash
# rollback batcher config
redwoodctl deploy rollback batcher-service --to-revision v4.12.1
# temporarily scale nodes
redwoodctl infra scale nodepool batchers --count +2
```

maya: Follow-ups for next shift:
- Li to finish postmortem input and link perf diffs (RW-OPS-1298).
- Alex to propose autoscaler tune (cooldown/step-size) and test in staging (RW-OPS-1301).
- Sam to write a short alert refinement to avoid pages for short-lived cache spikes (threshold + sustained window).

li: Notes for postmortem: include affected customer list (anonymized), token-cost delta during incident, and time-to-detect. I have partial logs in `s3://redwood-ops/logs/INC-2026-249/` for correlation.

alex: Escalation/Customer comms: CX sent a tentative incident banner to a few impacted teams; no broad outage banner required. If anything reappears, we should prep an apology + summary.

sam: Any unresolved technical debt? We still need: better KV eviction metrics, and a simulated churn test in staging. Adding to RW-OPS-1302.

maya: Thanks all. Handoff complete. Sam is primary, Li is secondary for next 8 hours. Ping in-thread if anything new. :thumbsup:

li: A couple of inline items I'll tackle today:
- Add `eviction_rate` to the critical dashboard.
- Add a canary test for small-batch fallback.

alex: Filing the reminder — sync at 12:30 to check whether autoscaler tuning reduced p95. I'll stay reachable until 08:30.

incidentbot: Incident INC-2026-249 status changed: RESOLVED by li at 03:08 UTC.

sam: Copy that. Will run a quick health sweep at 09:00 and update here.

maya: Closing note: great triage overnight. Keep follow-ups tracked in RW-OPS-1298/RW-OPS-1301/RW-OPS-1302.

alex: End of thread.
